corrections.original: R1/XCON, written by John McDermott at CMU in OPS5 ... grew from ~500 rules (July 1980)
corrections.fix: Begun Dec 1978 in OPS4 (250 rules Apr 1979, 750 Oct 1979); used at DEC since Jan 1980; rewritten in OPS5 from Apr 1980 (500 rules), 850 end-1980, ~2,000 mid-1982, ~3,300 Nov 1983; 6,200 in 1987 with ~50% changing yearly confirmed.

corrections.original: In 1987 Jack Schwartz became head of DARPA's IPTO
corrections.fix: Office was ISTO (IPTO's successor); start year contested (1986 per his biography, 1987 per AI-winter article citing McCorduck). 'Clever programming' / 'deeply and brutally' remain secondary, attributed paraphrase of McCorduck.

corrections.original: Weizenbaum ... calling the Japanese ambition 'as absurd today as it was twenty-five years ago'
corrections.fix: Quote verbatim and date 27 Oct 1983 confirmed, but 'That ambition' is Simon & Newell's 1958 forecast (which he links to Fifth Generation claims); 'solution looking for problems' concerns schools.

corrections.original: Q20 Dreyfus, 'Alchemy and AI' (RAND 1965): 'exhibits a recurrent pattern: early, dramatic success...'
corrections.fix: Verified wording is 'recurring pattern' in What Computers Can't Do (1972, reprinted 1992); RAND 1965 wording unverified - do not quote as from the RAND paper.

corrections.original: Fifth Generation ran 1982 to 1992 ... about ¥54 billion
corrections.fix: IPSJ: ~¥54bn over 11 years, 1982-1992; Wikipedia: 1982-1994 incl. follow-on, <¥57bn (~US$320M); IPSJ Fuchi page says finished 1993 (fiscal). Five PIM models, PIM/p 512 processors confirmed. Use 'about ¥54 billion over the main project, 1982-1992'.

corrections.original: UK Alvey Programme (from 1983; £350M proposed) ... evaluators judged commercial impact disappointing
corrections.fix: Hansard: accepted April 1983, director in post 1 June 1983, £200M government + £150M industry; Wikipedia says 1984-1990. Commercial-impact verdict could not be re-read (sources unreachable) - keep as secondary.
MCC ceased operations in 2000 (board voted to dissolve June 2000) and was formally dissolved in 2004.
Year 1991 confirmed; exact day not found in Schmidhuber's pages - use '1991'.

corrections.original: ALV work cancelled in April 1988; none of the SCI flagships delivered in promised form
corrections.fix: April 1988 only via Paleofuture blog citing Roland & Shiman; Project MUSE review blocked. Keep as secondary; 1983-1993 and ~$1bn confirmed.

corrections.original: R1: two earlier DEC attempts in FORTRAN and BASIC had failed
corrections.fix: Not found in Wikipedia XCON or Bachant & McDermott 1984; marked UNVERIFIED.
